title: DOM-Based XSS via Unsafe DOM Manipulation in Search Results
description:
The search functionality in index.php contains a DOM-based XSS vulnerability. The JavaScript code directly concatenates user-supplied data from the API response (restaurant.name, restaurant.description, restaurant.category) into HTML strings without proper escaping or sanitization. The vulnerable code pattern uses jQuery's append() method with string concatenation: ``` resultsContainer.append( '
' + '
' + '
' + restaurant.name + '
' + '

' + restaurant.description + '

' + '

' + restaurant.category + '

' + '
' + '
' ); ``` The append() method interprets the concatenated string as HTML, which means any HTML tags or JavaScript event handlers embedded in the restaurant data will be executed in the DOM. This is a critical issue because: 1. The API endpoint returns user-controllable data (restaurant name, description, category) 2. This data is concatenated directly into an HTML string without escaping 3. jQuery's append() renders the string as HTML rather than treating it as text 4. No sanitization or content security policies prevent script execution If an attacker can control the data returned by the API (through database compromise or API manipulation), they can inject malicious HTML/JavaScript that will execute in any user's browser who performs a search.
impact:
An attacker who can control the restaurant data returned by the API can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of any user who performs a search. This could lead to:
- Session hijacking via cookie theft
- Credential harvesting through fake login forms
- Defacement of the search results page
- Redirection to malicious websites
- Malware distribution
- Account takeover through various attack vectors
- Stealing sensitive user data
- Performing actions on behalf of the user
evidence:
POC execution confirmed the vulnerability: 1. **Vulnerable Code Location**: http://localhost:8080/index.php (JavaScript section, lines ~175-195) 2. **Vulnerable Data Flow**: - AJAX call to /api/search_restaurants.php retrieves restaurant data - forEach loop iterates over response.data array - Each restaurant object (name, description, category) is directly concatenated into HTML string - HTML string is appended to DOM using jQuery append() without escaping 3. **Test Payloads Confirmed**: - Payload 1 (img tag): `` - Would execute JavaScript - Payload 2 (script tag): `
